title: AI fabrication suspected of writing dozens of articles in Canadian publications

reading.body:
This is an impersonation failure at the point of authorship. A fabricated columnist identity was used to place dozens of articles in Canadian outlets over nearly two years, and the persona existed only as an email correspondent who refused video calls. The byline, not the copy, was the deceptive artefact, and the outlets published it under their own editorial standards.

The failure sits at the gatekeeping stage of publication, where a contributor's identity is normally verified before a byline is granted. Catching it would have required confirming that the person named in the byline existed independently of the email account, which the refusal of video calls made difficult but not impossible. A forensic check on the headshot, which later found it 97 percent AI-generated, was available as a verification step and was not run before publication.

What is not established is who operated the persona or why, and the reporting describes suspicion and an alleged campaign rather than a finding of intent. The complaint filed at an Istanbul courthouse is a complaint, not a ruling, and the outlets' removal of the articles is an editorial decision rather than an adjudication of the claims they contained.

reports.title: Exclusive—Fake AI columnist dupes Canadian press to target Moroccan dissidents, and a Turkish 'middleman'
Why we took down an article published under the name Daniel Robson
A statement on articles by ‘Daniel Robson’
Byline or bot? AI-generated ‘journalists’ start to appear in Canada
AI fabrication suspected of writing dozens of articles in Canadian publications

summary:
A fake AI-generated columnist named Daniel Robson infiltrated Canadian news outlets for nearly two years, publishing dozens of articles pushing narratives against Moroccan dissidents. The persona targeted Canadian-Moroccan businessman Hicham Jerando and former Moroccan intelligence officer Mehdi Hijaouy, and also attacked a Turkish textile supplier named Fuat, whose only connection was doing business with Jerando. Robson communicated only by email, refused video calls, and his headshot was confirmed by forensic analysis to be 97 percent AI-generated. The alleged financial evidence involved small transfers of $1,500 to $2,500, inconsistent with claims of a global drug empire.

After Türkiye Today raised questions, Canadian outlets including the Ottawa Citizen and Policy Options removed Robson's work, with Policy Options admitting a vetting failure. The Western Standard withdrew his articles three weeks later. Fuat faced doxxing, harassment, and threats, filed a complaint at an Istanbul courthouse, and sought psychiatric care. Robson denied being fake and accused Türkiye Today of endangering him.
